about: Clips and plates for the landing-page climb. Scenes are described in docs/design/scene-plan.md. A shot runs only when its status is "approved". Routes and prices are in scripts/generate-assets.mjs and docs/design/generation-models.md.

defaults.suffix: Photoreal, documentary, natural light, soft contrast, true colour, fine film grain. One continuous shot, slow and physical camera move, no cuts. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, neon, lens flare, bokeh circles, light orbs, purple, glowing orbs or rockets. Phone and laptop screens are never visible to the camera.
defaults.stillSuffix: Shot on a full-frame camera, natural light, soft contrast, true skin texture with pores and fine detail, true colour, subtle fine film grain, editorial documentary photograph. No text, letters, numbers, logos, crests, brand marks or watermarks anywhere, including on clothing, signs and devices. Phone and laptop screens are never visible to the camera. No purple, neon or lens flare.

shots.prompt: 6:10 a.m., before dawn in Palo Alto. One continuous 12-second shot that starts exactly on this image. Seconds 0 to 4: the camera holds still outside the kitchen window; inside, the girl finishes pouring coffee into her travel mug and screws on the lid; the reflection of the oak branches drifts slightly on the glass. Seconds 4 to 12: the camera pulls back from the window and rises slowly and steadily, a smooth crane move straight up: past the red tile roof of the Spanish-revival house, past bare oak branches, above a quiet street of large homes with a few warm windows, up toward a low layer of soft cloud in the deep blue pre-dawn sky, ending just beneath the cloud.

@Image1 is Ava, a 16 year old girl. @Image2 shows the exact shuttle interior, her seat, clothes and light. One continuous 10-second shot at 6:52 a.m. Seconds 0 to 3: a tracking shot alongside the moving shuttle on a country road at sunrise, the camera keeping pace just outside its side windows; thick oak trunks pass between the camera and the shuttle in the foreground, sweeping across the frame, and between them we glimpse Ava through the window, the glass bright with the reflected sunrise. As one wide oak trunk passes close to the lens and fills the frame for an instant, the camera is now inside the shuttle, seated beside her, exactly as in @Image2. Seconds 3 to 7: she works on her phone held low in her lap, screen never visible to the camera, one white earbud in; a tiny frown, a tap, a small nod. Low sun strobes across her face as trees pass. Seconds 7 to 10: she looks up and out of the window; the camera drifts past her shoulder to the glass and tilts up into the open dawn sky. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Ava's mother. @Image2 shows the exact car, school, clothes and light. One continuous 8-second shot at 3:15 p.m. on a bright winter afternoon in California. Seconds 0 to 2: locked close on the SUV's windshield; in sharp focus, the reflection of blue sky and live-oak branches on the glass; behind it, soft and out of focus, the driver. The focus slowly pulls through the glass: the reflection melts into blur and she comes into sharp focus in the driver's seat exactly as in @Image2. This is a real lens focus pull, not a dissolve or cross-fade. Seconds 2 to 5.5: she reads the weekly update on her phone held facing her, screen never visible to the camera; her shoulders drop a little, a small relieved smile; she sets the phone face down on her knee and looks out at the school. High school students aged 15 to 18 walk past in soft focus. Seconds 5.5 to 8: the camera rises up and over the SUV roof; the circular drive and red tile roofs fall away beneath; it ends on clear blue afternoon sky. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Mateo, a 17 year old tennis player. @Image2 shows the exact courts, bench, clothes and golden-hour light. One continuous 8-second shot at 4:35 p.m. Seconds 0 to 2: extremely close on his dark sunglasses, the lenses reflecting the golden sky; he lifts them off slowly and the camera eases back to reveal him on the courtside bench exactly as in @Image2. Seconds 2 to 5.5: he types one short message on his phone with his thumb, screen never visible to the camera, then slips the phone into his bag. That is all he does. Seconds 5.5 to 8: the camera tilts slowly up past the court light pole into a warm amber sky. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Priya, a 16 year old girl with glasses. @Image2 shows the exact bedroom, lamp and light. One continuous 8-second shot at 8:05 p.m. Seconds 0 to 2: close on her bedroom window from outside at night; in sharp focus, the reflection of the navy sky and the first stars on the glass; behind it, soft, the warm room. The focus pulls through the glass and she comes into focus at her desk, seen from a three-quarter angle, the plain back of her laptop lid at the frame edge with no logo. This is a real lens focus pull, not a dissolve or cross-fade. Seconds 2 to 6: she is in a live online class. She listens with a calm, still face, then answers in one short, calm sentence: small, natural mouth movements at a slow speaking pace, restrained expression, no exaggerated face or chin movement. Seconds 6 to 8: the camera drifts back and up away from the window into the night sky with the first stars. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is David, a Korean-American tutor in his thirties. @Image2 shows the exact home office, white linen-shaded lamp, microphone and light. One continuous 8-second shot at 9:00 p.m. Seconds 0 to 2: close on his office window from outside at night; in sharp focus, stars reflected on the dark glass; behind it, soft, the warm room. The focus pulls through the glass and he comes into focus at his desk exactly as in @Image2. This is a real lens focus pull, not a dissolve or cross-fade. Seconds 2 to 6: he explains something into the microphone at a calm, natural pace, one easy open-hand gesture, a slight smile; small natural mouth movements; the monitor faces him, screen never visible. Seconds 6 to 8: the camera arcs slowly to the window and up into the starry night sky. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Ava (cream cable-knit sweater). @Image2 is Clara, a Chinese-American girl (grey quarter-zip). @Image3 shows the exact SAT check-in lobby, proctor, phone bin and steady flat grey morning light. One continuous 10-second shot at 7:40 a.m. on a Saturday in early March. The light stays exactly the same flat grey daylight for the whole shot, no change in brightness or colour. Seconds 0 to 3: close on Ava's hand holding her phone; she holds the side button and the dark screen stays dark; she lowers it into the clear bin beside the other phones and lets go. Seconds 3 to 6: the camera rises to her face: she shows a plain card to the proctor, who nods; Ava breathes out once, and walks with Clara toward the glass door of the testing room. Seconds 6 to 10: they go in; the glass door swings closed toward the camera, and the closing glass fills with the reflection of the pale grey sky from the tall lobby windows; the camera rises with the reflection until the frame is only pale grey sky. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Mateo, now 18. @Image2 shows the exact Harvard Yard gate, his crimson HARVARD sweatshirt, tennis bag and early-September light. One continuous 6-second shot. Seconds 0 to 1.5: close on an old wavy pane of a brick dormitory window, in focus, reflecting elms and sky; the camera slides off the window and the focus moves to him walking through the brick and iron gate exactly as in @Image2. Seconds 1.5 to 6: he walks into the Yard at a natural pace, looks around once with a quiet half-smile, and keeps walking under the elms. The HARVARD lettering stays crisp and readable. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Priya, now 18. @Image2 shows the exact Stanford Main Quad arcade, her cardinal STANFORD sweatshirt and golden light. One continuous 6-second shot on a late-September afternoon. Seconds 0 to 1.5: close on the plain dark sunglasses pushed up in her hair, the lenses reflecting palm trees and sandstone arches; the camera eases back to reveal her under the arcade exactly as in @Image2. Seconds 1.5 to 6: she looks up at the arches with a calm, quiet face, lips closed, barely a smile, then turns and walks out into the sunlit quad. The STANFORD lettering stays crisp and readable. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.

@Image1 is Ava, now 18. @Image2 shows the exact UC Berkeley steps, her navy BERKELEY hoodie, Sather Tower behind her and morning light. One continuous 6-second shot on a late-August morning. Seconds 0 to 1.5: close on a shallow puddle on the granite steps, in focus, reflecting the blue sky and the white tower; her sneaker steps into it and the ripples break the reflection; the camera tilts up to her walking up the steps toward the camera exactly as in @Image2. Seconds 1.5 to 4: she climbs at a natural pace, calm, the BERKELEY lettering crisp and readable. Seconds 4 to 6: the camera rises over her head and tilts up the tall white tower to its spire and on into deep blue sky. The final second is only sky: no land, no buildings, no person in frame. All movement is real-time and natural, unhurried, nothing rushed or exaggerated.
